_description: Conduit saddle clamp, 68.4 x 80.0 x 31.2 mm, PETG. An inverted-U body straddles a 30 mm conduit and is through-bolted to a panel by two outward feet (drilled on assembly, so the printed body carries no holes). Printed feet-down on a 220 x 220 x 250 mm machine with a 0.4 mm nozzle. The cross-section is constant along the conduit, so the solid is a prism; the top corners of the opening are chamfered at 39.8 deg from vertical, which keeps every unsupported face inside the 45 deg rule AND cuts the flat ceiling down to an 18 mm bridge. Service load is drag along the conduit, which runs in the layer plane and so is not carried by the layer bonds. Every gate in this pack passes on this projection: it is the GOOD design the negative controls in selftest/bad_params.py and selftest/bad_meshes.py are measured against, each of which changes exactly one of these numbers.

_notes.part_bbox_mm: [x, y, z] extent of ONE PRINTED PART, in its PRINT ORIENTATION with the bed at z=0, mm. Read by fdm.bed_fit and by fdm.process_model_valid's unit check. Matches selftest/baseline_part.stl exactly. NOT the assembly envelope: cad-solid reads that, under assembly_bbox_mm, and the two were the same word until a 480 mm assembly got measured against a 220 mm bed. Falls back to bbox_mm / bbox / footprint_mm, in that order; write fdm.part_bbox_mm when another pack wants the same word.
_notes.part_volume_mm3: Solid volume of THIS PART, mm^3. 39.3 cm^3. Not the extruded volume - the gate applies shell and infill itself, and not the assembly's total material volume, which is what cad-solid means by volume_mm3. Falls back to volume_mm3 / solid_volume_mm3.
_notes.surface_area_mm2: Total surface area, mm^2. Optional, and it sharpens fdm.print_time_est: with it the shell volume is perimeters x extrusion width x area instead of a flat 35% guess.
_notes.part_min_wall_mm: Thinnest section MEASURED anywhere in the part, mm. Here the 3.2 mm side walls - eight beads at the 0.4 mm nozzle. The limit is 3 x extrusion width = 1.26 mm. This is a reading off the geometry; cad-solid's min_wall_mm is the opposite kind of number, the thinnest wall a PROCESS allows, and publishing one under the name the other expects hands a gate a threshold nobody chose. Falls back to min_wall_mm / thinnest_wall_mm / min_feature_mm / min_section_mm.
_notes.mesh_path: The exported part mesh IN PRINT ORIENTATION WITH THE BED AT Z=0, relative to the pack root. Every angle the mesh gates report is measured in the frame of this file: a part exported in assembly coordinates gets a true answer about a pose nobody prints. Generated by selftest/baseline_mesh.py, which documents the geometry. A real project points this at its own build output.
_notes.mesh_paths: The PRINT SET: name -> mesh path, one entry per part on the plate. Two copies of the same clamp here, which is what printing two of them looks like. fdm.overhang and fdm.bridge_span measure EVERY entry and return ONE verdict that names the worst part and counts the set; a bare list of paths works too and takes each name from its filename. A set WINS over the single mesh_path when a project states both, and every multi-part verdict names the key it came from so the precedence is never something a reader has to guess. It is in the baseline because CI has to prove the many-part path PASSES a good design: the negative controls only prove it can fail, and a fold that failed everything would otherwise ship green.
_notes.bed_x_mm: Usable bed X of the machine, mm. A property of the printer, not the part.
_notes.bed_y_mm: Usable bed Y, mm. bed_xy_mm is accepted instead for a square bed.
_notes.bed_z_mm: Z travel of the machine, mm. The brim costs nothing vertically, so height is checked against this raw.
_notes.brim_mm: Brim/skirt allowance per side, mm. fdm.bed_fit checks the footprint against bed - 2 x this, because the brim is what fouls a bed clip four hours into a print.
_notes.nozzle_d_mm: Nozzle orifice diameter, mm. Sets the minimum-wall table and is range-checked by fdm.process_model_valid (0.25-1.2 mm).
_notes.extrusion_width_mm: Slicer line width, mm. 1.05x the nozzle, which is what a stock profile ships. Overrides the nozzle table in fdm.min_wall; must stay inside 0.8-2.0x the nozzle or the wall rule is being applied to a bead it does not describe.
_notes.layer_height_mm: Layer height, mm. 0.50x the nozzle - inside the 0.10-0.75x band where the bead still gets squished into the layer below it, which everything this pack says about strength and bridging assumes.
_notes.perimeters: Wall loops the slicer will lay down. Count, not mm. Used by fdm.print_time_est for the shell volume; 3 is also the minimum fdm.min_wall enforces.
_notes.infill_fraction: Infill density as a fraction, 0-1. 0.35 for a clamp that is bolted up and carries load.
_notes.print_speed_mm_s: Nominal printing speed, mm/s, not the machine's maximum. 50 is an ordinary PETG figure. The estimate derates it by a 0.55 duty factor for travel, acceleration and cooling holds.
_notes.filament_density_g_cm3: Filament density, g/cm^3. 1.27 is PETG; PLA is 1.24, ABS/ASA 1.04-1.07, TPU 1.21. Only used to turn extruded volume into grams.
_notes.max_print_time_h: Ceiling on a single uninterrupted print, hours. 24 is the domain default; raise it only with a runout sensor and a reason.
_notes.max_filament_g: Ceiling on filament consumed by one uninterrupted print, grams. 1000 is one standard spool - past it the print needs a spool change or a splice mid-part, which is a different and worse problem than a long print. fdm.print_time_est fails on whichever of this and max_print_time_h is closer.
_notes.build_axis: Build direction in the part frame: an [x, y, z] vector, or an axis NAME ('z', '+Z', '-y'). +Z here, which is the default. Every overhang angle and the layer-alignment angle are measured against it.
_notes.load_axis: Primary service load direction in the part frame: an [x, y, z] vector, or an axis NAME ('z', '-y') - a string used to read as absent and reported 'the projection has no load_axis' to someone who had set it. +Y here, along the conduit: the clamp reacts drag in shear through its bolt feet, and that load runs in the layer plane rather than across the layer bonds.
_notes.utilisation: Structural utilisation from whichever gate computed it, as a ratio of allowable. 0.62. fdm.layer_alignment divides it by the directional knockdown and fails past 1.0 - it does not compute this number, it derates it.
_notes.utilisation_kind: Which quantity 'utilisation' is: 'stress' or 'deflection'. It selects the knockdown - strength is roughly half across the layer bonds, stiffness is about 0.85 - and the gate refuses to guess, because guessing is a 1.7x error either way. A key named deflection_utilisation is taken at its word without this.
_notes.layer_normal_strength_ratio: Layer-normal tensile strength as a fraction of in-plane strength. 0.5 is the middle of the 0.35-0.7 band across common filaments and ordinary settings. Applied to a STRESS utilisation.
_notes.layer_normal_modulus_ratio: Layer-normal elastic modulus as a fraction of in-plane modulus. 0.85: stiffness is far less anisotropic than strength, because the weld is nearly as stiff as the bead until it starts to open. Applied to a DEFLECTION utilisation.
_notes.overhang_limit_deg: Steepest face the machine prints without support, degrees from vertical. 45 is the conservative classic. The worst face on this part is the 39.8 deg opening chamfer.
_notes.overhang_area_allow_frac: Fraction of total surface area allowed past the overhang limit, 0-1. 0.005 is small enough that a real unsupported region trips it and large enough that tessellation slivers do not.
_notes.bridge_ceiling_deg: Angle at which a downward face stops being an overhang to support and becomes a ceiling to bridge, degrees. At or past 80 it belongs to fdm.bridge_span, below it to fdm.overhang.
_notes.max_bridge_mm: Longest unsupported horizontal span the machine will bridge acceptably, mm. 30 is where a well-cooled bridge is still flat enough to build on. This part's ceiling spans 18 mm because the chamfers ate the rest. Applies to a ceiling anchored on OPPOSITE sides, where the strand is pulled taut between two landings.
_notes.max_cantilever_mm: Longest unsupported horizontal projection off a SINGLE anchor, mm. 2.0 - a cantilevered strand has no second landing to pull against, so it droops and curls from the first pass instead of pulling straight, and a couple of millimetres is what cools before it sags. A bridge limit applied to a cantilever passes a shelf hanging in mid-air; this part has no cantilevered ceiling at all.
